title: Data-driven equations reveal rainfall-linked North Atlantic decadal variability
summary: Using SINDy equation discovery on monthly observational indices from 1950–2022, researchers derived three linked low-order equations for Atlantic Multidecadal Variability, the North Atlantic Oscillation and North Atlantic precipitation. The model recovered a distinct roughly 20-year component and highlighted precipitation-linked terms as robust components of the learned dynamics; tests against the independent 1900–1939 record found skill for statistics of the variability indices and rainfall. The equations generate hypotheses about ocean-atmosphere feedbacks; they do not establish a single causal mechanism or guarantee forecasts.
ai_technology: Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) equation-discovery algorithm
organization: University of Oxford; UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology; UK Met Office

evidence.tested: Using SINDy equation discovery on monthly observational indices from 1950–2022, researchers derived three linked low-order equations for Atlantic Multidecadal Variability, the North Atlantic Oscillation and North Atlantic precipitation.
evidence.unknown: The learned equations are compact models/hypotheses from observational associations. The paper and Oxford source note that proposed mechanisms need further evaluation; reported hindcast skill is not prospective climate prediction validation.
evidence.ai_role: Searched candidate dynamical models against observational time series and selected sparse, interpretable coupled equations; the researchers analyzed robust equation terms and compared the resulting model against a historical holdout period.
